task: T4: honour a pause intent, in scripts/ralph-build.sh. When the polled action is `pause`, the loop holds before starting the next unit of work instead of proceeding: it keeps writing its heartbeat so a reader can see it is alive, marks the phase as paused so a paused run is visibly paused rather than indistinguishable from a hung one, and re-polls on a sleep interval rather than spinning. It leaves the hold when the action becomes anything other than `pause` — carrying on when there is no action, and cancelling when the action is `cancel`, using the cancel behaviour T3 already built rather than a second copy of it. A paused loop must remain interruptible by the ordinary means and must not hold a lock or a temp resource that a human would have to clean up. Change nothing about how the intent is fetched; T3 owns the fetch, and this task owns only what the loop does when the answer is `pause`.
